historical_exact_hash_comparison.interpretation: the reconstruction differs from the original beyond the two PE fields. Inputs the frozen record does not fix: (1) the embedded web UI: llama-server's build downloads UI assets from HuggingFace when it has network access (tag b<build number>, then latest); the reconstruction builds had none and embedded 0 assets, while the historical build may have embedded a UI -- the likely main cause; (2) llama.cpp clone depth, which sets LLAMA_BUILD_NUMBER (here 1) in version strings and in the UI tag; (3) the original source path and the user-owned toolchain prefix (only __FILE__ strings). The mechanism that injected the _WIN32_WINNT define is shown immaterial: a variant build with the define in the C++ flags only gave byte-identical objects and the same normalized llama-server.exe (ggml.h defines _WIN32_WINNT 0x0A00 when unset). None of these is an R2-12 code change, and none touches the /health and /completion paths, token output or the expert-store decode path that G1 compares; the exact cause is not proven and the original normalized digest is unknown

g1_relationship: R5-00 DECISION_RULES gates.G1_implementation requires that A on the R5 build produce tokens identical to 'the pre-R5 runtime (llama-research-v5)' and be no more than 2% slower. The comparator is the pre-R5 v5 implementation, not a byte sequence; no frozen R5-00 artifact names the binary hash. The hash 65f445c4... is named by the R5-01 Phase 1a artifacts (llama-research-r5-ets/BUILD-INFO.json predecessor_runtime, host_conformance.py V5_SHA256) as the identity of that reference; both stay unchanged, and this manifest adds the single reconstructed identity next to it. The reconstruction is the v5 implementation built from the v5 commit with the recorded v3..v5 toolchain and configuration (the same toolchain and flags as the R5 build), so G1 still compares R5-A with the pre-R5 runtime. host_conformance.py records which identity (historical or reconstructed) was used in IDENTITY.json and G1_HOST_RESULT.json.
disclosures: The original binary cannot be recovered; the reconstruction is not byte-identical to it beyond the PE timestamp and checksum (see historical_exact_hash_comparison).

The v3..v5 CMake flags were never recorded for those builds: they are taken from tools/build_llama_research.sh at 34997c2 (also recorded verbatim in llama-research-v2/BUILD-INFO.json) plus the disclosed _WIN32_WINNT deviation. The historical builds ran the same compiler packages from a user-owned prefix (GCC_EXEC_PREFIX/--sysroot/-B); the reconstruction uses the packages installed normally.

llama-research-v5 was built at 2026-11-14T20:18Z, about 90 s before commit 34997c2 (20:19:33Z); the reconstruction assumes the built working tree equals the commit (its BUILD-INFO describes exactly the committed change).

The compiler's host libraries (isl, mpfr, gmp of the Ubuntu 24.04 build host) and the historical CMake/Ninja versions are not pinned or recorded; the compiler identity string and the package hashes are.
Model-free regressions ran on a synthetic store, not on the real Qwen store.
The driver hashes the comparator once per run (unchanged behaviour) and records the identity in IDENTITY.json, not in every launch record.
